item.title: ATLAS finds hints of the hidden structure of the vacuum
item.description: Researchers at the University of Bonn, together with colleagues from Oxford and Prague, played a leading role in analyzing particle collisions at CERN's Large Hadron Collider. The ATLAS Collaboration observed more proton collisions with the particle pattern it was looking for than expected. This could point to a phenomenon predicted by the Standard Model of particle physics that has never been directly observed, known as QCD instanton processes. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ozone hole one of the largest in decades
item.description: In contrast to the 2025 seasonal ozone hole above Antarctica, which was the fifth smallest since 1992, this year's ozone hole ranks as one of the largest in 48 years, based on long-term atmospheric observations, including data from the Copernicus Sentinel-5P satellite. While this may sound alarming, it is important to remember that the size of the ozone hole varies naturally from year to year, and the long-term recovery of the ozone layer remains on track. item.title: The dark matter puzzle deepens: Nearby galaxies challenge cosmic simulations
item.description: Galaxies appear to hold a surprise beneath their visible stars: Their inner regions contain less dark matter than some of our most advanced simulations predict. Dark matter is invisible, but its gravitational pull helps govern the motions of stars and gas. By measuring these movements, astronomers can reconstruct where this unseen matter lies and test the computer simulations used to understand the universe. A study of 136 nearby galaxies, involving the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (IAC), reveals a discrepancy that becomes more extensive in more massive systems, offering fresh clues… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why fertile male killifish outlive their peers
item.description: Why do some individuals of the same species live significantly longer than others? In evolutionary biology and aging research, this question is often linked to a trade-off between reproduction and survival. The underlying idea is that energy and resources invested in reproduction may lead to compromises in repair and maintenance, thereby hindering a long life. Thus, the assumption is that particularly successful reproduction at a young age comes at the cost of a shorter lifespan. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Meteor blast scars hint at Venus's gradual volcanic makeover

The fainter outer halo spans some 180 kilometers (110 miles), yet there is no obvious crater at the center. A space rock may have created the entire pattern by exploding in the planet's thick atmosphere. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The faintest supernova ever observed refuses to go out, staying visible for nearly a year
item.description: An international team of astronomers, including Paul Groot of Radboud University, has discovered that a supernova explosion does not always have to be extremely bright. The team has identified the faintest supernova observed to date. It remained visible for an exceptionally long time and appears to have been caused by a so-called white dwarf and a relatively small companion star. The discovery may have implications for our understanding of the evolution of binary stars and the measurement of the expansion of the universe. The results were published in Nature Astronomy. item.description: a ball will fall. trade on where it lands. I made this game! Some technical details: The entire drop of the ball is simulated server-side, then streamed to each client as server-sent events with a small buffer. Every drop is deterministic from its starting position, so rounds can be replayed exactly for later analysis, but tiny variations in starting position can change the ultimate outcome. There's some AI traders to keep the market moving, but they drop out in any round that has more than five people. item.title: Breathing less oxygen tripled lifespan in mice with a deadly brain disorder
item.description: Oxygen is essential for life, but too much of it can become dangerously toxic, particularly in people with certain neurological and mitochondrial disorders.
